narration: The arm does not resist the dagger. The slip opens flat. Two instructions occupy the same paper in different inks. The older hand reads: “Living occupants first to dry galleries; sealed records to tannery loft.” The correction reverses them: “Sealed voices first; living occupants hold Low Sluice.” Its ninth word is warmth. The doubled wax belongs to the Crier’s Circle, but the correction is signed only by a blank oval—and when your candle turns, every raised letter casts a tiny shadow except that mark. On the back, a fresh wet line has appeared: SHELTER IS A KIND OF DOOR.

payload.what: The original Low Sluice order prioritized living occupants; a second hand reversed it to prioritize sealed records, used 'warmth' as the ninth word, and signed with a shadowless blank oval.

ruling.understoodAction: Manipulate and inspect the offered document without placing Mira's hand in the sorting mechanism.
ruling.ruling: The dagger method safely turns an exposed slip. Reading visible writing, seals, corrections, and signature needs no check.
ruling.stakes: The document links the evacuation fraud to the local shadow-for-warmth myth and has just written a new line in response to the crisis.
